facts.statement: The genus Serratolamna was described by Landemaine in 1991.
The known fossils of Serratolamna primarily consist of teeth and scattered vertebrae.
facts.quote: The fossils of Serratolamna mainly consist of teeth and scattered vertebrae.

facts.statement: Serratolamna teeth were asymmetrical, featuring smooth crowns and multiple cusplets.
facts.quote: The teeth are asymmetrical with smooth crowns and multiple cusplets.

facts.statement: The basal margin of Serratolamna tooth roots was V-shaped.
facts.quote: The basal margin of the roots are V-shaped.

facts.statement: Based on tooth size, Serratolamna likely grew no larger than 1.5 metres.
facts.quote: Based on the size of its teeth, it appears Serratolamna grew no larger than 1.5 metres.

facts.statement: Serratolamna fossils have been found in the Late Cretaceous of Cuba, France, Madagascar, Mexico, Morocco, Sweden, and the United States.
facts.quote: Fossils of species within this genus have been found in Late Cretaceous of Cuba, France, Madagascar, Mexico, Morocco, Sweden and United States.

facts.statement: Serratolamna lived from the Turonian to the Lutetian stages, between 93.9 and 41.03 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Turonian to Lutetian (93.9 to 41.03 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Serratolamna is an extinct genus of mackerel sharks belonging to the monotypic family Serratolamnidae.
rejected.quote: Serratolamna is an extinct genus of mackerel sharks that is placed in the monotypic family Serratolamnidae.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'Serratolamna is an extinct genus of mackerel sharks'
